summary: Thomas Nathan Patton is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Cornell University, where he studied under Anne M. Blackburn, and held a post at the City University of Hong Kong (attested 2018).
Thomas Oberlies works in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Albrecht Wezler and held a post at the University of Freiburg (attested 2001).

Thomas P. Kasulis is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He held posts at Ashland University (circa 1980–1991) and Ohio State University, where he served as a professor from circa 1991 to 2018.

Thomas Watters (1840–1901) was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Queen's University Belfast in 1857 and completed a B.A. at Queen's University of Ireland circa 1857–1861.

Thomas William Rhys Davids (1843–1922) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Waskaduwe Subhuti, Yataramulle Dhammarama, and Adolf Friedrich Stenzler at the University of Breslau, later holding posts at UCL and the University of Manchester.
Thomas Zehnder is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Zurich under the supervision of Alexander Lubotsky.

Thomé H. Fang (1899–1977) specialized in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at National Central University from circa 1929 to 1948 and at National Taiwan University from circa 1948 to 1973.

Thubten Yeshe (1935–1984) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and Trijang Rinpoche, and held posts at the University of Virginia (1982) and Middlebury College (1982).

Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (1946–2023) was an active figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Thubten Yeshe (circa 1959–1984), Trijang Rinpoche (circa 1959–1981), and Denma Lochö Rinpoche, and co-founded Kopan Monastery by 1971.

Thupten Jinpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and the University of Cambridge, later holding posts at Girton College, Cambridge (circa 1996–1999) and the Institute of Tibetan Classics (circa 1999).

Théodore Pavie (1811–1896) was a scholar of Indology and Sinology. He studied under Eugène Burnouf, whom he succeeded at the Collège de France (1852–1857), and later held a post at the Catholic University of the West (circa 1875–1896).

Thích Minh Châu (1918–2012) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University (circa 1961–1964) and served as a lecturer in Chinese at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 1984).
Thích Thiện Châu (1931–1998) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He completed his studies at Paris-Sorbonne University (circa 1967–1971) and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (circa 1973–1977).

Tianshu Zhu specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Northwest University (MA) and Ohio State University (PhD under John C. Huntington), holding posts at Northwest University, Shaanxi History Museum, Ohio State University, and Korea University.

Tilak Kariyawasam works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as head of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and as Dean of the Graduate School at the International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

Tilmann Vetter (1937–2012) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner and Erich Heintel, and served as a professor at Leiden University from circa 1973 to 2002.

Tim Dean studied at the University of East Anglia under Robert Clark, Brandeis University, and Johns Hopkins University. He held academic posts at the University of Washington, the University at Buffalo, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

Timothy H. Barrett specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Yale University and the University of Cambridge, and held teaching posts at the University of Cambridge (attested 1981) and SOAS University of London (from 1986).

Timothy Lenz works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon and Collett Cox, and later held posts there, including as a professor (attested 2017).
Timothy Lubin is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Columbia University in 1994 and held a post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2020).
